Ubuntu uses the device proxy explicitly

Only new Ubuntu sessions use the proxy address and protocol configured in the network trust section below. Off by default; the device must provide the proxy, and nothing is injected when the address is unset. TLS verification is not disabled.
Optional · off by default · applies on next backend start

Only appends trust to the newly started OpenCode Web backend and its child processes; default roots are preserved. Android / WebView, the standalone terminal, Ubuntu and the system store are not modified. This CA can sign certificates for any site, so verify the file SHA-256 through an independent trusted channel; nothing is downloaded automatically and TLS verification is never disabled.

Selection cleared; the old copy remains for a running service. After a backend restart trust is no longer appended.
Existing services unchanged; stop and restart the OpenCode service from home.
Backend uses the device loopback proxy

Only a newly started OpenCode backend injects proxy variables for the address configured below. The address supports http:// and socks5://. Off by default; the device must provide the local proxy, and nothing is injected when the address is unset. TLS verification is not disabled; certificate trust remains controlled by the custom CA above. Stop and restart the service from home after changing.
OpenCode service in Ubuntu PRoot · experimental

Only newly started OpenCode backends run through PRoot inside the Ubuntu development instance. Session tools come from the guest. If the instance is missing, the first service start extracts it from the embedded archive; this takes several minutes and requires sufficient storage. Errors are reported. Enable the network proxy and custom CA separately as needed. Stop and restart the service from home after changing.
